newsitem.title: POLAND: DERIVATIVES SEEN DRAWING MORE CAPITAL TO POLAND.
newsitem.headline: DERIVATIVES SEEN DRAWING MORE CAPITAL TO POLAND.

text.p: Polish analysts and officials said the planned launch of derivatives on East European indices in Austria could lure fresh capital to Warsaw as it would give investors a chance to hedge their Polish investments.
Austrian futures and options exchange Oetob said on Monday it would start offering derivatives on its Polish, Czech and Hungarian stock indices from March 20.
Artur Czerwonski, an analyst at Pekao SA brokerage said the derivatives trade on Polish index, would make investing in Polish stocks less risky and therefore more attractive.
"Foreign institutions might now lack instruments to hedge their risks and derivatives might let them safely expand their positions in shares with purchases of...futures or options," he said.

The deputy president of the Warsaw Stock Exchange saw the start of the derivatives trade as a boon for the Warsaw bourse and saw no danger of shifting investors' interest from shares into derivatives.

"I don't think investors would withdraw from their shares in Warsaw to invest in derivatives, as holding shares gives them dividends and impact on managing companies, which derivatives don't," Piotr Szeliga said.
Szeliga said the Warsaw bourse should itself be able to start with its blue-chips index WIG 20 futures in the second half of the year, possibly in the third quarter.
He said the next stage would likely be introducing options but said it would be possible only in the second half of next year.

"We would think about options, but rather on shares than on the index, I think it would be possible only next year, possibly in the second half of 1998 as the market has to learn derivatives and it will take time," he said.
